subject: Currency repricing + tax entity liaison for GCP Marketplace May invoice
messages:
From: procurement@globex.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@globex.com, gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com
Date: 2028-05-30T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy on May GCP marketplace invoice — currency & VAT allocation

Hi Soojin,

We got the May GCP Marketplace invoice (attached) and noticed two issues: first, several line items that were previously billed in GBP were repriced in EUR, and second, VAT was charged to our UK entity instead of our EU subsidiary (we're registered in IE for marketplace transactions). The net effect is an overpayment of ~€18,600 in VAT rounding and currency conversion.

Please advise immediately: we need a) a provisional credit while you confirm the correct entity mapping, and b) confirmation you will coordinate with Google to apportion charges to the IE entity for future invoices.

Attached: Globex-May-2028-invoice.pdf, entity_certificate_globex.pdf

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Procurement, Globex Corp.
procurement@globex.com

P.S. Accounts payable flagged a ‚stop payment‚ on the invoice until this is resolved — happy to provide any docs you need.

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: procurement@globex.com
Cc: gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on May GCP marketplace invoice — currency & VAT allocation

Hi Samir — thanks for flagging and for the attachments. Im looping in our finance lead (Marissa) and marketplace ops (Karthik) so we can move fast.

Immediate asks so we can escalate to GCP and issue a provisional credit:
- Confirm the exact invoice number you placed on stop-pay (we see several similar IDs)
- Confirm your IE VAT registration number (we have the entity certificate but need VAT reg to reassign tax)
- If possible, share the PO/contract line that specifies billing entity (we can attach it to the marketplace dispute)

Our proposed path: Redwood issues a provisional credit for the VAT overcharge amount (subject to reconciliation) within 3 business days of receiving the VAT reg + invoice ID; we will simultaneously open an entity reallocation request with Google Cloud Marketplace. GCP typically takes 30–45 days to process apportionments, but we will push for priority review.

Marking this high priority — Marissa, Karthik: can you confirm provisional credit authority/channel? I will prepare the formal request to GCP with the attachments once I have the VAT reg number and invoice ID.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Renewals & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal - Globex May invoice: provisional credit & GCP liaison (do not forward)

Team — quick internal plan before I send the external confirmation:

Background: Globex was billed in EUR for lines that historically invoice in GBP; they claim VAT was assigned to the wrong legal entity (UK instead of IE). Net VAT overcharge est. €18.6k. Globex put a stop-pay on the invoice.

My ask / checklist:
- Marissa: confirm we have latitude to issue a provisional credit for up to €20k under our Marketplace refund policy and provide the ledger accounting code. We should issue as a contra-revenue item; finance will reverse if GCP apportionment arrives and settles differently.
- Karthik: prepare the GCP escalation bundle (invoice PDF, entity_certificate_globex.pdf, PO if they provide it). Use the priority template (Subject: Marketplace APPORTIONMENT REQUEST — Redwood/Globex).
- I'll draft the external confirmation to Samir that we will issue a provisional credit within 3 business days pending the VAT reg + invoice ID, and that we'll open the GCP request in parallel.

Risks: if GCP declines apportionment we may be liable to reclaim the provisional credit; include language in the credit terms about reconciliation. I attached a short draft of provisional_credit_terms.docx (internal) — please review 2 hours.

If you have no objections, I'll send the confirmation to Samir now and open the GCP case.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, procurement@globex.com
Date: 2028-06-01T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace apportionment inquiry — invoice MAY-2028 (next steps)

Hi Soojin / Samir,

Thanks for the details. We can support an entity reallocation for Marketplace charges but need the following to begin the process:
1) Seller account ID and Marketplace invoice number (as issued on the PDF)
2) Signed confirmation of the target legal entity (VAT registration number + certificate)
3) Any customer PO or contract reference that indicates legal entity preference (helps speed review)

Once we receive these items we will create an internal apportionment ticket. Typical handling time is 30–45 calendar days for cross-entity VAT reallocations; in cases with provisional credits issued by the seller, we can prioritize and attempt a 20–30 day window.

Note: GCP cannot effect refunds on behalf of the seller; we can reassign charges and issue ledger adjustments on the marketplace statement. Please coordinate the provisional refund through Redwood (seller).

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Google Cloud Marketplace Billing
gcp-marketplace-billing@google.com
